title: Wait for execution
description: Bounded wait (at most 30 s) until the execution is terminal, or until it pauses for your repair of a failed block (pause.kind agent-repair, or pause.handoff under a sign-in wall: answer with dsagent.execution.handoff.get / resume / abort).
guidance: A run in this browser is followed from its own runtime without backend polling and reports progress with movedDuringWait; call again while terminal (not status) is false, then follow nextActions.

executionId.description: Opaque workflow execution identifier to poll.

timeoutMs.description: Bounded wait duration in milliseconds; defaults to 30000.

runToken.description: The run's ownership token, as dsagent.execution.run or dsagent.wizard.run returned it (shown once). Pass it when your browser connection was renewed (a restarted Connector): the run, its open repair handoff and its pages follow you to the new connection. Not needed on the connection that started the run.

inputSchema.description: Execution and maximum duration for one bounded status wait.

status.description: Current execution status: the backend record's word (pending, running, success, completed, failed, cancelled, stopped, restricted, partial). dsagent.execution.get / wait of a run paused in this browser give its pause word instead: paused-agent-repair, paused-auth-interrupt or paused-resource-pressure. Plan on lifecycle and terminal. partial: saved rows without collecting everything (the agent repair handoff ended it, or it finished short of its collection: errorCode COLLECTION_PARTIAL; terminal).

startedAt.description: Optional execution start time, UTC ISO 8601 (for example 2026-11-01T09:01:56.000Z).

finishedAt.description: Optional execution finish time, UTC ISO 8601.

durationMs.description: Optional execution duration in milliseconds; absent while unknown.

endpoint.description: The typed place the failure of the run landed on, from one closed set: target-* (the step's element), wait-timeout / readiness-* / block-timeout (waiting), navigation-* / new-tab-* / tab-unavailable, effect-unverified (a click or upload that may have happened: inspect the page before acting again), collection endpoints (record-limit-not-reached, records-not-saved, traversal-budget-exhausted), input and host endpoints, plan-restricted (a plan limit, named in endpointDetails.planRestriction), plan-check-unavailable (the plan check did not answer: no limit), unclassified. Absent when the run did not fail, or failed outside this browser.

endpointFallback.description: The last fallback tier the endpoint admits: recovery (the in-run repair already tried), agent-handoff (an agent may repair it), person (a wall the person passes), none (terminal).

kind.description: Which detail this is: navigation, readiness, budget, tab, timeout, recorded-target, effect, detail-visit, auth or plan.

planRestriction.description: plan: the plan limit the server named (AUTOMATION_DAILY_LIMIT, AUTOMATION_CONCURRENCY, PLAN_EXPIRED, ...).

wallType.description: auth: the kind of sign-in or verification wall the run waited out (LOGIN_FORM, CAPTCHA, SSO, ...).

failureClass.description: navigation: the browser failure class (dns, connection, offline, timeout, certificate, blocked, http-error, ...).

transient.description: navigation: whether waiting can clear it.

reason.description: readiness: the readiness reason; tab: closed, discarded, frozen or no-tab.

resumeCursor.description: budget: the opaque point the chunked read paused at; a handoff retry continues the read from it.

timeoutMs.description: timeout: the deadline that passed, in milliseconds.

awaitedState.description: timeout of a wait for an element: the state it waited for (visible, hidden, attached, ...).

matched.description: timeout of a wait for an element: elements its selector matched at the deadline (a selector that matched is not stale).

visible.description: timeout of a wait for an element: how many of the matched elements were visible.

attempts.description: timeout (block-timeout): how many attempts the block ran before its deadline.

waitingOn.description: timeout (block-timeout): the page command the block was still waiting on (a command type such as LOOP_ELEMENTS).

lookalikes.description: recorded-target: elements on the page that look like the recorded target.

fields.description: detail-visit: the detail fields the visit was to read.

read.description: detail-visit: how many of them it read (0: the visit read nothing; its record is not saved until you answer).

endpointDetails.description: Bounded, value-free detail of the endpoint; never page text, URLs or selectors.

endpointProvenance.description: How the endpoint was known: typed by its owner, a stable code, or read from an untyped message.

errorCode.description: The terminal error code of the endpoint (NODE_* for a node, ENGINE_ERROR, SQLITE_SCHEMA_WRITE_UNCONFIRMED, PLAN_RESTRICTED).

errorNodeId.description: The workflow node the run failed at; read it with dsagent.workflow.definition.get.

outcomeSource.description: Where how-it-ended was read from: local (the run executed in this browser; everything is its own), or backend (the run executed elsewhere; the DSphere backend stored its endpoint, node, row count and coverage, or only its error code for a run reported before the endpoint travelled).

stopSource.description: A stopped run: who stopped it. person (the SidePanel), agent (dsagent.execution.stop), tab-closed (its page was closed), server (the backend), chat-task (the Chat task that ran it was cancelled), plan (the plan automation limit was reached; endpoint plan-restricted), unspecified.

handoffEnding.description: How a run that took the agent repair handoff's terminal path ended it: aborted (dsagent.execution.handoff.abort), timed-out (the handoff deadline passed), budget-exhausted (no handoff left), handoff-disabled (the run was started with agentRepairHandoff false). With rows saved the run is partial, without them failed.

decline.description: Why the in-run recovery did not repair the failure.

recovery.description: The in-run recovery the run tried for the failing node; present when it declined.

rowsSaved.description: Distinct records committed to the local data sheet; they are kept after a failure.

rowsUnsaved.description: Rows whose write to the local data sheet was still not confirmed after the bounded retry of the buffered writes of the run; they stay queued for a later recovery. Absent when every write confirmed.

rowsRecovered.description: Rows a retry of the buffered writes of the run saved after their first write failed.

status.description: Whether the collection reached what it asked for.

expectedParents.description: Parent records the detail loops listed to visit (all list pages, within the record limit).

visitedParents.description: Parent records whose detail visit ended, in sequential and parallel loops alike.

unresolvedVisits.description: Visits whose outcome could not be proven.

shortfallVisits.description: Visits that fell short of a strict record count.

skippedVisits.description: Visits whose loop item was skipped (skip-item, or a visit that never started): not collected; counted among the unresolved visits.

rowsVanished.description: Parent records the list loop listed that the list no longer showed when the loop read it again after the page shifted (a re-rendered or re-fetched list): still expected, never visited. The reason a run that visited every row left is partial.

requestShortfall.description: Lists that reached their verified end below the requested record count: their records are all there is (a record count is a cap, not a promise); the collection is not short for it.

lists.description: Lists that stopped before their end.

requestStoppedShort.description: Lists that stopped below the requested record count before their end was verified (a time or pass ceiling while they still grew, a stalled pagination, a load still pending): they may hold more, so the collection is partial.

advertised.description: Records the list's own data response says the list has in all.

collected.description: Records the list gave before it reached its end.

advertisedTotal.description: The list reached its end with fewer records than the data the page received says it has in all (Settings → Network Data). It does not change status: a site's total often counts records it never shows. Look at the page when the difference matters.

advertisedMore.description: Present and true when the list reached its end on the page while the newest data response the page received for it still said there are more records (a has-more flag). It does not change status; the page may have stopped loading early. Look at the page when it matters.

status.description: Whether every reply thread (nested parent: the replies under a comment) the run saw was proven read to its end. partial makes the collection partial even when every visit ended.

resolvedParents.description: Threads proven read to their end.

unresolvedParents.description: Threads it could not prove read to their end; their replies may be incomplete.

uniqueChildren.description: Distinct replies the threads were proven to show.

mainListExhausted.description: Whether the list holding the threads was read to its end.

unresolvedReasons.description: The unresolved threads counted per reason, most first.

reason.description: Why the threads stayed unresolved: not-visited (never opened), parent-* (the comment could not be identified or found again: unavailable, identity-unavailable/-ambiguous/-mismatch, binding-unavailable, not-accepted, unresolved), child-readiness-unresolved / rows-unresolved / identity-ambiguous (its replies could not be identified), control-absent, child-pagination-pending (it still showed a control for more replies), child-rows-unaccepted, child-page-cycle, child-payload-incomplete (a field of its replies was not read), evidence-limit, parent-time-slice-budget / parent-no-progress-budget / visit-ceiling-reached (a bound ended its visits), revisit-no-progress / bounded-revisit-exhausted (reopening it added nothing), other.

items.description: One reason and how many threads it left unresolved.

parents.description: Threads whose page showed a reply count above the replies the run accepted.

children.description: Replies those counts exceed the accepted ones by, in all.

advertisedShortfall.description: Threads whose own reply count says replies are missing; a page may count replies it no longer shows.

truncated.description: Whether the thread evidence was cut at its bound.

nestedCoverage.description: The reply threads behind the collection status: counts and typed reasons, never their content. Present when the run read replies under a list.

truncated.description: Whether the evidence was cut at its bound.

collectionFulfillment.description: Collection completeness, separate from the run status.

fieldsMissing.description: Fields the run saved its records without, counted per field: detail fields its detail visits missed, fields the wizard showed with a value that read empty on every row of the run (degraded outcome field-empty-all-rows: the run saved its rows, but that column is lost), and list fields whose match in a record was another field by its stated label or place, left empty rather than read wrong (degraded outcome field-identity-refused, counted in rows; check the page before trusting the data), and list cells left empty although the record shows the field (degraded outcome field-read-blanked, counted in rows). A visit that read none of its fields is handed to you instead (endpoint detail-visit-unverified, endpointDetails.kind detail-visit).

items.description: One detail field and how many records lack it.

chartsIncomplete.description: Chart fields whose sweep could not prove it read every record the chart shows (degraded outcome chart-sweep-incomplete): a gap between neighbouring readings stayed open, the time limit cut the sweep, or it found about one record per pixel of the plot (the pointer moves in whole pixels, or the chart draws a sample of its series). The run saves the records it read (within its record limit), so a success can still be a partial chart: compare with the chart (for example a narrower date range) before treating the data as the whole series. Absent when every chart read was complete.

count.description: Records the incomplete sweep read; the chart may show more. The run saves them within its record limit (rowsSaved), so it can save fewer.

items.description: One chart field and how many records its incomplete sweep read.

filled.description: Fields with cells the run saved from the data the page itself received: the page showed the cell empty, or cut its text short.

empty.description: Cells the page showed empty, saved with the page data value.

truncated.description: Texts the page cut short, saved whole.

items.description: One field and how many of its cells were completed.

differs.description: Fields with cells whose page value differs from the data the page received. The page value is what the run saved; look at the page if the difference matters.

items.description: One field and how many of its cells differ.

uncheckedRecords.description: Records that matched no single record of the data the page received, so their values were saved as the page shows them, unchecked.

structureChanged.description: Fields the data the page received no longer has: they were saved as the page shows them. Running the scrape wizard again restores the check.

notRead.description: Fields the page does not show (source network) that stayed empty in every record: the data the page received was not read in this run, because the person switched Network Data off or the page gave none. The page fields were saved as usual.

networkData.description: What the run did with the data responses the page itself received (Settings → Network Data): counts per field, never a value, address or path. Absent when the run checked nothing.

failed.description: Requests of the page itself that were answered with an error, or not answered at all, while the failed step ran.

client-error.description: Answered with another client error (status 400 to 499).

server-error.description: Answered with a server error (status 500 or above).

network-error.description: Not answered at all (a network error).

kinds.description: The same requests by kind; only kinds that happened.

pageRequests.description: On a failed run: the page's own requests that failed while the failed step ran, from the page's request log. Evidence beside endpoint, not the endpoint: rate-limited or refused requests suggest the site held the page back, and a later run may fare better. Counts only, never an address or a message.

itemsSkipped.description: Loop items answered skip-item in a repair handoff (by you or the person): not collected, and no row was written for them. Absent when none was skipped.

nodeId.description: The node the run stopped at.

stoppedAt.description: Where the run stopped collecting, when it failed or ended partial at a node.

degradedOutcomes.description: Lesser outcomes the run kept instead of failing.

kind.description: kept-unreached (a read kept its empty value), zero-iterations (a list loop ran no item), continued-unverified (a click meant to open a tab opened none), pagination-shortfall (pages ran out before the requested count), rows-not-saved / rows-unverified (the local sheet), detail-field-missing (a detail visit kept its record without this field), item-skipped (a loop item answered skip-item: not collected, no row written), field-empty-all-rows (a field the wizard showed with a value read empty on every row; count is the rows saved without it), field-identity-refused (a list field whose every match in a record was another field, by its stated label or its place in the record; the cell stayed empty; count is the rows), field-read-blanked (list cells left empty although the record shows the field: the recorded field refused the value at its place, or recovery found several candidates; count is the rows; check the page before trusting the column), chart-sweep-incomplete (a chart field whose sweep may have missed records; count is the records it read; see chartsIncomplete), parent-not-accepted (replies the reply loop read under a comment the run could not read as a row: held by no row and not saved; count is the replies), records-read-not-saved (a run that did not succeed read list records it never saved; count is the records read beyond the rows saved), records-not-saved (a run that succeeded collected list records its confirmed saved rows do not hold; count is the records collected beyond the rows saved; the run ends partial), parents-not-visited (a detail loop ended before visiting every parent record it listed; count is the parents never visited; see collectionFulfillment), response-filled-empty / response-filled-truncated (cells the page showed empty or cut short, saved with the value of the data the page itself received; see networkData), response-differs (cells whose page value differs from that data; the page value is saved), response-records-unchecked (records that matched no single record of that data), response-structure-changed (a field that data no longer has), response-field-not-read (a field the page does not show stayed empty: that data was not read in this run).

endpoint.description: The endpoint the step would have failed on.

nodeId.description: The first node it happened at.

field.description: The variable or column the kept value belongs to.

coverage.description: What the run collected and where it stopped; present when the run executed in this browser.

siteResponsiveness.description: Present only while something is wrong with how websites answer this task's tab; absent when they answer normally. site-slow: the website itself is slow, stalled, failing, rate-limiting or unreachable while other websites in the same tab answer normally, so it is not a browser or Agent fault. local-network-slow: every website is slow alike, so it is the person's network or proxy. Either way: do not switch browsers, reload the extension or repeat actions faster; tell the person once which website is slow, then wait (dsagent_page_wait) and read again. DSphere never changes its own timeouts because of it.

verdict.description: site-slow: the website is the problem; local-network-slow: the person's network or proxy is.

reason.description: What is wrong: slow answers (median wait 3 s or more), requests waiting over 10 s, failing requests (5xx or connection errors), rate limiting (HTTP 429), or the website cannot be reached.

host.description: Host name of the tab's website; never a path or query.

medianWaitMs.description: Median time the website took to start answering over the last 20 s; absent when no request answered.

stalledRequests.description: The website's requests waiting more than 10 s without an answer (long polls excluded).

failedRequests.description: The website's requests that failed in the last 20 s.

sampledRequests.description: The website's requests counted in the last 20 s.

controlMedianWaitMs.description: Median wait of the other websites the same tab loaded over the last 60 s (the comparison); absent when none answered.

hint.description: One sentence on what to do.

count.description: How many failures the run passed over, such as detail visits whose page did not open; each such record is kept with empty detail fields.

firstError.description: The message of the first failure the run passed over.

toleratedFailures.description: Failures the policies of the run tolerated (skipped list items). The run went on and its status is unchanged; present only when there were any and the execution ran in this browser.

hasResult.description: Whether at least one execution result artifact is available.

artifactCount.description: Number of listed artifacts when the execution is terminal and artifact access is available.

savedFiles.description: Confirmed local files saved by this run. Explicitly tell the person these locations. For more than 50 use dsagent.artifacts.list.

filePath.description: Actual local file path, including browser fallback naming.

lifecycle.description: The lifecycle to plan on, whatever words status (the backend record) uses: completed covers completed and success, partial is a run that saved rows without collecting everything: it ended through the agent repair handoff (you aborted it, its deadline passed, its handoff budget was spent, or the handoff was turned off), or it finished short of its collection (errorCode COLLECTION_PARTIAL: parents it listed and never visited, visits unresolved or failed, fewer records than requested, records skipped; coverage says which; coverage that is only unknown keeps completed) (coverage.rowsSaved; they are kept and listed like any terminal run's, and endpoint names where it stopped), failed covers failed and restricted (refused under the plan limits), stopped covers stopped and cancelled, paused is a run in this browser waiting on a sign-in wall, on host resources, or on your repair of a failed block (pause says which).

kind.description: What the run waits on: auth = a sign-in or verification wall (see waitingOn); resource = host memory or CPU pressure, it resumes on its own; agent-repair = a block failed after every automatic tier and the run waits for your answer (dsagent.execution.handoff.get, then dsagent.execution.handoff.resume or dsagent.execution.handoff.abort) until deadline.

waitingOn.description: Who the run waits on. auth: person (the wall is theirs; never sign in yourself); agent = a verification challenge on the page of your run is yours to try, as a page read of pageContextId says (attemptsLeft); once it is gone the run resumes by itself. resource: host (the pressure must ease, or the person adjusts the resource-pressure settings). agent-repair: agent = you (the person may also answer in the SidePanel; the first answer wins); person = your control session ended and did not come back within 30 s, so the person answers in the SidePanel until deadline (moved earlier, at most 5 minutes); you may still answer while it is open. A run you did not start (openedFor person) waits on the person from the start.

openedFor.description: agent-repair: whom the handoff was opened for. agent: the agent that started the run (you, when you did). person: nobody started this run over MCP or the Chat (a SidePanel start, a dataset run, a scheduled fire); the person answers in the SidePanel within 5 minutes and you cannot answer it.

attemptsLeft.description: auth with waitingOn agent: effect calls you may still spend on the challenge before the person takes it over.

sinceMs.description: auth, resource: how long the run has waited, in milliseconds.

deadline.description: ISO time. auth: the run ends failed on auth-required if the person has not passed the wall by then (60 minutes; a restart keeps it). resource: the pause is escalated to the person then (escalated true); the run stays paused. agent-repair: the run ends failed on the block's endpoint if you have not answered; it stands still while a sign-in wall outranks the handoff.

type.description: The kind of wall (LOGIN_FORM, CAPTCHA, SSO, ...).

host.description: The host of the walled page.

retryAfterMs.description: With type RATE_LIMITED: the wait the site asked for, in milliseconds, when it named one.

wall.description: auth: which wall stands, on which host.

pageContextId.description: auth: the run page the wall stands on, issued to you to observe (never to sign in on), and to act on while waitingOn is agent. agent-repair: the run page the block failed on, issued to you (the agent that started the run): observe and act on it with dsagent.page.* while the run waits.

handoff.description: auth: the repair handoff the wall outranks, still open and still yours to answer (the same fields as an agent-repair pause: handoffId, endpoint, nodeId, blockType, attempt, deadline, answers, retargetable, pageContextId). Its deadline stands still while the wall stands; answer it once the person passed the wall, or now.

trigger.description: resource: which host resource is under pressure.

memoryPercent.description: resource: host memory in use when last sampled.

cpuPercent.description: resource: host CPU in use when last sampled.

escalated.description: resource: the pause outlasted its deadline; the person was told again. The run is still paused; the way out is nextStep.

kind.description: resource: the typed way out: adjust the resource-pressure settings (thresholds, or turn the pause off) with the person's agreement.

settingsSection.description: The settings section to read with dsagent.settings.get and change with dsagent.settings.update.

capability.description: The capability that applies the change.

nextStep.description: resource: what ends the pause other than the pressure easing.

handoffId.description: agent-repair: the handoff to answer with dsagent.execution.handoff.get / resume / abort.

endpoint.description: agent-repair: the typed execution endpoint the block failed on (the same enum terminal runs report).

blockLabel.description: agent-repair: its label in the workflow.

targetDescription.description: agent-repair: the element the block was recorded on, as a person names it (role and label); never a selector.

attempt.description: agent-repair: the run's how-many-th handoff (at most 5 per run, 1 per block and loop item).

loopNodeId.description: The loop block whose item failed.

loopItem.description: agent-repair: the loop item the block failed in, when it ran in a loop.

answers.description: agent-repair: the answers this handoff accepts (skip-item only inside a loop item).

retargetable.description: agent-repair: whether retry may rebind the block to another element (retarget.pageTargetId): the block recorded an identity to verify it against.

restored.description: agent-repair: the handoff was open when the Extension restarted and was restored with the same handoffId and deadline.

pause.description: Present while the run is paused in this browser: what it waits on, who must act, and until when.

terminal.description: true: the run has ended (completed, partial, failed, restricted or stopped) and its artifacts are final; false: wait again or read progress. A failed or partial run names its endpoint, errorNodeId, recovery and coverage.

resultDelivery.description: Present when the run ended in this browser and its result is still on its way to the DSphere backend: the run is terminal and its status, finishedAt and durationMs (which end when the run ended) are its own. The backend's execution history and its copy of the result follow once delivered; nothing is needed from you.

items.description: A page context of a tab the run holds.

runPageContextIds.description: The pages of the tabs this run holds right now (its worker tabs, popups and stamped tabs), issued to you as your pages: read them with dsagent.page.observe, and close one the run left behind with dsagent.page.close once the run ended. Absent when the run holds no tab, does not run in this browser, or another agent started it (its tabs stay with that agent).

currentNode.description: The node running now, when the runtime names one.

nodeIndex.description: One-based position of the current node among the nodes of the run.

recordsSoFar.description: Records the run has scraped so far (detail records included).

authInterrupt.description: Present while the run waits on a sign-in or verification wall the person must pass.

paused.description: Present while the run is paused for host memory or CPU pressure; it resumes on its own.

movedDuringWait.description: execution.wait only: whether the records, node or status of the run changed during this wait. false on a run that is not terminal means it made no visible progress for the whole wait (a stall, a hidden window, a wall): read progress and the page of the run before waiting again.

progress.description: Present while the run executes in this browser: what it is doing now. A run elsewhere (another browser, a server) carries no progress.

nextActions.description: What to call next, in order. Terminal: read the result (dsagent.artifact.read, dsagent.execution.data.export, dsagent.artifacts.list; empty when the run left no result); never wait again. An open repair handoff that is yours to answer: dsagent.execution.handoff.get, then resume or abort. A sign-in pause of your run: wait, or dsagent.execution.auth.resume once the person says they signed in; a challenge yours to try (pause.waitingOn agent): read pause.pageContextId, pass it, wait. Otherwise (running, pending, a wall or a handoff the person answers): dsagent.execution.wait.

items.description: One capability to call next, as the catalog names it.

warnings.description: EXECUTION_ALREADY_TERMINAL: you waited on a run you were already told has ended. The reply is the same outcome; stop waiting and follow nextActions. Plan on the code, never on the message.

code.description: Stable warning code to plan on.

nextActions.description: What to call instead of waiting again, in order.

items.description: One capability to call next, as the catalog names it.

timedOut.description: true: the wait used its whole timeoutMs and the run has not ended; wait again. false: the run is terminal, or the wait returned early with something to act on: a repair handoff it had not returned before (pause), or the end of the handoff it returned last time. A wait on a handoff it already returned waits until that handoff is answered or replaced.

rows.description: Terminal wait with a local dataset: its first records (at most 20, at most 16 KiB), as dsagent.artifact.read returns them.

rowCount.description: With rows: how many records the dataset holds.

artifactId.description: With rows: the dataset rows came from.

rowsTruncated.description: With rows: true when rows holds fewer records than rowCount; rowsRest reads them all.

rowsRest.description: Only when rowsTruncated: the call that reads every record. Send it as it is (dsagent_invoke method and args), then repeat it with args.cursor = nextCursor until eof.

format.description: JSON Lines pages of whole records.

siteKnowledgeAsk.description: Present (on the reply that hands the task its data, and on the finish) when this task used a site no earlier run taught you about and recorded nothing for it. If you learned how the site works, call dsagent.site.knowledge.record once per site with its pageContextId: it still takes a record for 5 minutes, at the revision of its last observation. Optional; never data.

note.description: What to do with the sites.

sites.description: The sites, each with the last page the task used there.

revision.description: The revision of its last observation, for entries that name a targetId.

outputSchema.description: Execution state after the bounded wait; a terminal run with a local dataset carries its first rows.
